item.title: notes on editing ruthlessly
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
I keep coming back to editing ruthlessly, so here are the notes I wish I had earlier.

why it matters

Editing ruthlessly shows up across writing work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Optimise for the reader who shows up six months from now with no context.
  • Prefer the obvious solution; clever costs interest forever.
  • The fix that survives is the one the next person can understand.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

item.title: on editing ruthlessly
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
A quick write-up on editing ruthlessly, mostly so future me stops relearning it.

why it matters

Editing ruthlessly shows up across writing work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Write it down once, link to it everywhere.
  • Most of the value is in deleting, not adding.
  • If it is hard to test, that is the design telling you something.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

item.title: editing ruthlessly, revisited
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
Short post: editing ruthlessly is one of those things that looks simple until it isn’t.

why it matters

Editing ruthlessly shows up across writing work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Name it after what it does, not after how it does it.
  • Start with the smallest thing that works, then make it boring on purpose.
  • Make the default path the correct path so nobody has to remember the rule.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.
